snippet: Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move. Agentic VLMs have recently brought large improvements on such tasks by letting the model actively gather evidence with 3D perception tools instead of answering in a single pass. title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
snippet: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states. However, exposing this complete context uniformly at every step ignores that relevance is transient and sparse: the signal determining one action can become clutter at the next. Because executed actions feed back into the context, these errors compound into Sequential Distraction, driving the agent into irreversible trajectory drift. summary: A paper proposes 'Focused Perception' for omni-modal GUI agents, selecting only the relevant parts of streaming screenshots, audio, video and history at each step to avoid compounding 'Sequential Distraction' and trajectory drift.

title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
snippet: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. summary: SolarRenderer is a few-step, structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two LoRAs to render realistic video from engine or agent-specified scene structure.

title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
snippet: Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. For sequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of the recurrent state. summary: Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR) trains looped language models so each iteration matches the state after k operations and rescales recurrent state norms, improving length generalization on state tracking with a Qwen2.5-0.5B model.
whyItMatters: It addresses why extra test-time loops often fail to help on longer problems.

title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records
snippet: Enterprise agents answer questions over workplace records that evolve through team collaboration. As information is shared, corrected, and revised across documents, chats, and figures, multiple versions of the same information accumulate in the workspace. Reliable question answering therefore requires agents to reason over sufficient evidence, resolve cross-source and temporal conflicts, and recognize when the available evidence is insufficient to establish an answer. summary: MMEnterprise-Bench is a benchmark of 1,613 questions testing enterprise agents on evolving multimodal workplace records, including resolving conflicting versions and recognizing insufficient evidence.

title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
snippet: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter, an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading. summary: Specter speeds MoE inference with offloaded experts by using a quantized draft model for multi-step lookahead over expert usage, hiding PCIe transfer latency.
whyItMatters: It could make running large MoE models on limited GPU memory more practical.
